title: Build kernels and see the kernel trick
brief: Compute RBF and polynomial kernel matrices with one matrix product, then confirm that a degree-2 polynomial kernel equals a dot product of six explicit features.
hints: For rbf_kernel, build the squared distances as a column of squared row norms plus a row of squared row norms minus 2 * X1 @ X2.T. Use [:, None] and [None, :] so the sum broadcasts to an (n1, n2) table, then clip at zero before exp.
polynomial_kernel is one line: add coef0 to the matrix of dot products, then raise every entry to the degree. Do not power X1 itself.
For poly_features_degree2, slice the two columns of X once, then stack six columns: 1, sqrt(2) x1, sqrt(2) x2, x1^2, sqrt(2) x1 x2, x2^2. Dropping a sqrt(2) is the usual reason the final check fails.
